hook.line: At a hearing, your opinion needs a proper opening. Spanish has a polished few, and they sound much better than starting every sentence with *yo pienso*.
hook.es: A mi modo de ver, la solución es evidente.
hook.en: The way I see it, the solution is obvious.

examples.es: A mi modo de ver, la solución es evidente.
examples.en: The way I see it, the solution is obvious.

examples.es: Desde mi punto de vista, el proyecto es demasiado caro.
examples.en: From my point of view, the project is too expensive.

examples.es: Considero que la propuesta es justa.
Consideramos que el barrio necesita ayuda.
examples.en: We believe that the neighborhood needs help.

examples.es: A mi modo de ver, vale la pena salvar el edificio.
examples.en: The way I see it, it's worth saving the building.

examples.es: A nuestro modo de ver, el plan es injusto.
examples.en: The way we see it, the plan is unfair.

rule:
Open with your view, then a comma, then your statement.

*A mi modo de ver, …* and *Desde mi punto de vista, …* are neutral.
*Considero que…* and *Consideramos que…* sound more formal.
Change *mi* to *nuestro* or *su* to give someone else's view: *A su modo de ver…*.
After *considero que* the statement is plain: *Considero que es justa*. When you doubt, *no considero que* takes the subjunctive: *No considero que sea justa*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these opinion markers: set phrases that signal "this is my view, not a fact".

options: I consider the proposal fair.
We consider the proposal fair.
She considers the proposal fair.

readAndPick.es: Consideramos que el proyecto es caro.
options: I believe the project is expensive.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___, la solución es evidente.* (*A mi modo de ver* or *Según un estudio*) The way I see it, the solution is obvious.
yourTurn.answer: A mi modo de ver, la solución es evidente.
accept: A mi modo de ver la solución es evidente.
yourTurn.why: It is your own view, so *a mi modo de ver*; *según* is for someone else's.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ que la propuesta es justa.* (*Considero* or *Consideramos*) I consider the proposal fair.
yourTurn.answer: Considero que la propuesta es justa.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: From my point of view, the project is too expensive.
yourTurn.answer: Desde mi punto de vista, el proyecto es demasiado caro.
accept: Desde mi punto de vista el proyecto es demasiado caro.
yourTurn.why: The set phrase is *desde mi punto de vista*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We believe that the neighborhood needs help.
yourTurn.answer: Consideramos que el barrio necesita ayuda.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it formally: *A mi modo de ver, el plan es justo.* Use *considero que*.
yourTurn.answer: Considero que el plan es justo.
yourTurn.why: *Considero que* replaces the opening phrase and keeps the statement.

yourTurn.prompt: Change to *we*: *Considero que el plan es justo.*
yourTurn.answer: Consideramos que el plan es justo.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The way I see it, it's worth saving the building.
yourTurn.answer: A mi modo de ver, vale la pena salvar el edificio.
accept: A mi modo de ver vale la pena salvar el edificio.
yourTurn.why: Open with the phrase, then the statement.

pitfalls.wrong: En mi punto de vista, el proyecto es caro.
pitfalls.right: Desde mi punto de vista, el proyecto es caro.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "in my point of view", but Spanish uses *desde*.

pitfalls.right: Considero que el plan es justo.

pitfalls.wrong: Según mi modo de ver, el plan es justo.
pitfalls.right: A mi modo de ver, el plan es justo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The set phrase starts with *a*; *según* is for quoting someone else.

personal: Pick something in your town you have a view on, such as a park or a new building. Say your view with *A mi modo de ver…* and then once more with *Considero que…*.
